Several NHTSA campaigns cover this VIN's population: 21V424000 (6-cyl PCM shutoff/stall), 23V044000 (cam carrier oil channel), 26V389000 (driver airbag clockspring corrosion), 26V599000 and 26V248000 (DC/DC converter). 21V435000 applies only to Defender X with smoked lamps and likely not to this SE. Completion of any of these is unknown.
No scan is provided. The cluster photo shows a red warning triangle, so a full-system scan, including the 48V/BISG and air-suspension modules, is essential.

The seller claims a 'great service history', a transfer case service and a LiquiMoly oil service with an OEM filter. No receipts or intervals are shown. It is not stated whether the oil meets JLR spec.
The dealer says its inspection found a turbo coolant line leak and that it installed the updated-design lines. No repair order, part numbers or post-repair pressure test are provided.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is present: the VIN, a clean decode, a cluster photo matching the mileage and a stated clean title. The maintenance half is missing: no receipts, no dealer recall report, no scan, no coolant-line part numbers and no CPO paperwork.

condition.rationale: Photos show a clean interior with light wear and tires with good visible tread. However, a turbo coolant leak is disclosed (repair claimed but undocumented), a red warning triangle shows in the cluster, the dealer admits off-road use, and the underbody, air suspension and 48V system are unexamined.

price_value.rationale: The $32,975 asking price is above the $27,000 max_price in the budget, and no fair-value comps exist. Per the market notes, white cars at 88k+ trade at a discount, and 88k miles with undocumented 'lifetime' fluids implies catch-up work.

mission_fit.rationale: It does supply real capability the RX lacks: a low-range transfer case, a flat cargo floor for a sleeping platform and roof-rack potential. But the buyer context states Jason will not touch Land Rovers, his mechanic works on VW and recommends Toyota/Lexus, and the price sits above the budget band.

logistics.rationale: Bon Aqua, TN is a fly-and-drive trip from Carmel. A dealer seller and the nearby Nashville-area LR dealers make a PPI plausible, but PPI access is not stated. California registration of an out-of-state 2020 car needs an emissions-label and smog check.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A typical P400 SE with Meridian audio, a ClearSight mirror, a sliding panoramic roof and a contrast roof. White with no named packs (Off-Road, Explorer) is a common, less desirable spec.

evidence.mission_note: The Defender supplies genuine capability the RX lacks, but it conflicts with Jason's stated refusal to own a Land Rover and with his mechanic's Toyota/Lexus advice. The asking price also sits above his budget band.
evidence.rationale: The VIN decode and cluster photo establish a 2020 Defender 110 SE with the 3.0 I6 at 88,641 miles, consistent with the listing. Everything about maintenance is seller prose: the CPO status at 51k, the transfer case service, the replaced turbo coolant lines and the 'great service history' come with no receipts, part numbers or dealer printouts. Observed issues are a red warning triangle visible in the cluster photo, a dealer-disclosed coolant leak repaired without documentation, and the dealer's own admission of off-road use. Several recalls apply to this population, including a 6-cylinder PCM stall campaign, cam carrier oil leak, airbag clockspring and DC/DC converter, and their completion is unknown. Air suspension, 48V system health and ZF/differential fluid status at this mileage are unaddressed. The asking price is above the budget's max_price, and the brand conflicts with the buyer's stated Land Rover exclusion.
evidence.next_action: Ask the dealer for the LR dealer VIN recall/software report, a full-system scan explaining the red cluster warning, and the coolant-line repair order with part numbers before spending any time on travel or a PPI.
